## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
We have a static HTML project - just need index.html (+ assets). It auto-captures desktop and mobile screenshots. So the game must look good immediately on load, no external network dependency ideally (CDN may work? could fail in CI). Best to write self-contained Canvas 2D game with no dependencies. Given "4 vs 4 with roosters with super muscular human bodies and feathers" — a 2D arena brawler/shooter would be feasible and polished. Three.js via CDN is risky offline. Could vendor three? Not necessary. A stylized 2D canvas brawler can look excellent with procedural drawing.

Design: "GALLOS DE ACERO" / "COCKFIGHT COLOSSEUM" — 4v4 team battle, top-down/isometric-ish arena. Player controls one of 4 on blue team; 3 AI allies vs 4 AI enemies. Weapons:
- Corta distancia (melee/short-range): lanza huevos negros con lava verde — short-range weapon that throws black eggs trailing green lava (arcing projectiles).
- Largas (long-range): "unas mejores" — something better: "Plumas de Obsidiana" / long-range rail/beam? User sentence unfinished. Make long-range have better: "Huevo Ígneo Dorado" or "Pluma de plasma" — long-range weapon fires piercing golden feather spears / green lava laser beam. Give each character a weapon class: 2 short-range egg-lobbers, 2 long-range "Pluma de lava" rifles that fire piercing charged shots / triple spread.

Gameplay: top-down arena, WASD move, mouse aim, click shoot, Shift dash, Space special (Molotov egg / feather storm). Mobile: dual virtual joysticks with auto-fire. Health bars, respawns or first team to X kills. HUD scoreboard 4v4 with portraits, kill feed, round timer, win screen. Particles: lava splashes, green pools slowing/burning. Muscular rooster character art procedurally drawn: humanoid torso with pecs/abs, chicken head with comb/beak/wattle, tail feathers, wings as arms with gloves, drumsticks legs. That's fun to render. Need good visual quality.

Let me plan a solid architecture in a single index.html? Better split: index.html, style.css, game.js maybe multiple modules. Static server serves them fine. Keep files reasonably sized.

Let me design carefully:

Canvas 2D, resolution scaling. World ~1600x1000 arena viewed full? Fixed arena fitted to screen, top-down with slight pseudo-3D (draw shadows, scale characters). Camera: fits arena bounds on mobile; use a camera that follows player zoom on mobile? Simpler: arena fixed 1400x900, camera scales to fit viewport (letterbox with background). Mobile landscape? Portrait 390x844 - arena vertical letterbox. Better make arena responsive and camera follow with zoom capped. Let's implement camera centered on player with smoothing, zoom based on viewport: desktop show full arena? Full arena 1600x1000 at 1440x900 scale 0.9 fit; on mobile width 390 => scale 0.55 shows 700x1500 world, camera follows. Use camera zoom = clamp(min(w/1100, h/800), ...). Actually simpler: camera zoom = max(w/1500, h/1000)? That fits whole arena (zoom smaller). For mobile portrait, whole arena would be tiny. So use follow camera: zoom = clamp(w / 900, 0.5, 1.2) on mobile; desktop zoom = min(w/1500,h/1000) -> whole arena visible. Hmm gameplay needs awareness. Let's do zoom = clamp(Math.min(w,h)/700, 0.6, 1.1) on mobile portrait; camera clamped to arena. On desktop use fit-to-screen whole arena: zoom = min(w/1650, h/1050) but ensure at least 0.55. Arena 1600x1000 at 1440x900: min(0.87,0.857)=0.857 fits. Fine.

Actually maintain camera with follow for all and zoom based on viewport: desktop = min(w/1700,h/1050) (whole arena), mobile = min(w/850,h/900)?? For 390x844: min(0.46, 0.94)=0.46 too zoomed out. Use mobile zoom 0.7 and follow. Detect coarse pointer.

Combat:
- Player champion drawn, movement with acceleration, aim to mouse world.
- Enemies AI: seek to preferred range, strafe, shoot with cooldown, avoid pools, retreat when low.
- Allies AI same with team.
- Projectiles:
  - EggLob (short): slow big black egg, arcs with shadow, on land creates lava pool (green) dealing DoT and slow; direct hit damage.
  - Long-range: "Pluma Solar" — fast piercing lance of golden-green plasma? User says "las largas tengan unas mejores" (have better ones). Give long-range "Huevo de Lava Perforante" or "Pluma Ígnea": fast, pierces enemies, longer range, charged shots that explode? Keep distinct: long-range fires a golden-white/green "pluma de plasma" piercing shot, larger damage falloff? To be "better", long-range: higher damage, piercing, less cooldown? Balance with short: short has splash/pool area denial, high burst close range. Long: precise piercing rail shots with slower fire rate.

Weapon classes per fighter:
Team roster:
Blue team "Los Invencibles": 
1. REX (player): short-range, "Huevo de Obsidiana" double-shot lobber.
2. TITÁN: short-range, heavy "Huevo Fundido" triple spread.
3. VÉRTIGO: long-range "Pluma Ígnea" piercing beam rifle.
4. AZTECA: long-range "Garra Solar" 3-shot spread? Long range better: "Rifle Pluma" high-speed projectile.
Enemy team "La Yema Oscura": similar mirrored, different colors (red/purple).

Maybe simpler: two archetypes each team: 2 Brawler (short) and 2 Sniper (long). Player picks? Keep player as short-range main, since eggs are the signature. Could allow switch with Q? Nice: player can toggle character? In 4v4 you control one champion; switching would be weird. Add "choose fighter" start screen: 4 roosters, 2 short 2 long. Player selects, game starts after click. But auto-capture clicks start button — good. Need immediate attractive screen: title with roster and "JUGAR". Start overlay with character cards, weapon descriptions. Auto capture's start selector default? capture-start clicks heuristics likely a button. Let's check capture-start.mjs quickly to make sure.

Also mobile controls: left joystick move, right joystick aim+auto fire, dash button, special button. Must ensure start overlay tap works.

HUD: top bar team scores/kills, timer, 4 portraits each side with HP, kill feed, ability cooldowns bottom. Spanish text.

Round: first to 8 eliminations or 120s; respawn after 4s at spawn points. Winner screen with "Revancha".

Visuals:
- Arena: dark volcanic colosseum, stone tiles, lava cracks glowing, boundary fence, torches, crowd silhouettes? Top-down arena with hex/round platform. Draw:
  - Background dark gradient.
  - Arena ellipse/rounded rect floor with tile pattern, cracks with pulsing green lava.
  - Rings, corner braziers with glow.
  - Pools of green lava (animated).
  - Feather particles, embers.
- Characters drawn procedurally (top-down-ish angled front view?). Top-down games often draw characters from above; but cool muscular rooster needs side/front silhouette. Use "3/4 view": body seen from front while moving in 8 directions, flip horizontally for aim. Draw humanoid muscular torso, chicken head, wings-arms holding weapon, tail feathers behind. Slight bob and leg animation. This gives personality. Aim rotation only weapon; body flips.

Character render details:
- shadow ellipse.
- tail feathers: 3-5 arcs behind in team secondary color.
- legs: two thick drumsticks with talons, walk cycle.
- torso: broad trapezoid with skin/feather color, pecs shading, abs lines, feather tufts shoulders.
- arms: muscular biceps + forearm, gloves; holding weapon toward aim.
- head: rooster head with comb (red/orange), beak yellow, eye with angry brow, wattle.
- team accent: scarf/bandana, shoulder pads.
- health bar above; name label for player; small level badge.
- glow indicators.

Eggs: black shell with green glowing cracks, trail of green particles.
Long-range shots: bright golden feather-shaped projectile with green trail, piercing.
Projectile collision circle vs character radius.

Melee? "armas que las de corta distancia tiren huevos negros" — short distance weapons throw black eggs. So both archetypes ranged, short-range = lobbed eggs (limited range) with lava pools. Long range = better projectiles. Fine.

Special ability per archetype:
- Short: "Lluvia de Huevos" — 5 eggs in cone / around target.
- Long: "Pluma Penetrante" — charged beam/rail piercing all enemies in a line, high damage.
Dash for all (Shift / button).

Add damage numbers, hit flashes, screen shake, slow-mo on kill? Keep reasonable.

Audio: WebAudio synth for shots/hits, toggled by button; start on user gesture. Nice-to-have. Implement small synth.

Performance: particles cap.

Let's structure:
- index.html
- styles.css
- game.js (large, maybe split: engine? Keep single game.js ~1800 lines manageable). Use modules? Serving static works with <script type="module">. We can split into js/champions.js, js/engine.js etc. But writing many files with coherent integration is more work; single file ~2000 lines is okay but edit risky. Let's split logically:
  - js/main.js: setup, loop, input
  - js/render.js: draw arena & characters & effects
  - js/game.js: state, entities, AI, combat
  - js/audio.js
Maybe simpler to keep two/three files. I'll write game.js containing everything draw + logic (~1500 lines). Hmm, maintainability matters less; correctness matters. But writing long file in one write call is fine.

Let me plan constants and code carefully.

World:
const W=1600,H=1000; arena center (800,500), radius-ish rounded rect bounds x[120,1480], y[100,880]. Use rounded rectangle playable area via clamp and an ellipse? Collisions clamp to rounded rect (simpler): bounds margin 80 and ellipse check? Use rounded rect: clamp positions to [90, W-90] etc. Arena floor drawn as rounded rect.

Spawns: blue left (x 300) positions y 300/430/570/700; red right (x1300).

Units:
{
 id, team, isPlayer, archetype:'brawler'|'sniper', name, color(skin etc), x,y, vx,vy, r:26, hp,maxHp, aim, moveDir, facing, cooldown, dashCd, specialCd, alive, respawnT, speed, killer...
 stats derived from archetype:
  brawler: hp 150, speed 250, r 30, fire cd 0.62, projectile egg speed 520, range ~520, damage 26 direct + pool 18/s
  sniper: hp 120, speed 235, r 27, fire cd 0.95, projectile speed 1050, range 900, damage 34, pierce 2? Better long range: high speed, pierce 3, damage 30. Keep balance: brawler DPS ~42 + area; sniper 30/0.95=31 with pierce, but range advantage.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable web game: 4v4 arena combat with rooster-headed, hyper-muscular humanoid fighters; short-range weapons lob black eggs that burst into green lava; long-range weapons are stronger piercing plume shots.
- User request (Spanish, unfinished): "Hasme un 4vs 4 con gallos con cuerpo de humano super musculoso y con plumas y de armas que las de corta distancia tiren huevos negros como con lava verde y las largas tengan unas mejores".

## Requirements
- Build immediately without clarifying questions; note reasonable assumptions.
- Self-contained static game (no external assets/network dependencies).
- Must work on mobile (responsive, touch controls, safe areas).
- Spanish UI.
- 4v4, short-range egg/lava archetype and long-range "better" plume archetype.

## Decisions
- Pure Canvas 2D + ES modules, no frameworks or CDN assets.
- Player selects one of four blue-team roosters; 3 AI allies vs 4 AI enemies.
- Short-range: "Huevo de Obsidiana" lobbed black egg → green lava pool (DoT + slow); special = 5-egg fan.
- Long-range: "Pluma Ígnea" fast piercing plume with burn; special = piercing lava beam.
- First to 10 knockouts, 150-second timer; respawn after 4.4s; dash + special abilities.
- Mobile: dynamic dual joysticks (move/aim), auto-fire/auto-aim, DASH/SPECIAL buttons.
- Menu doubles as live attract-mode arena; Play button uses `aria-label="Play"` so automated capture can start it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full project scaffold: `index.html`, `style.css`, `favicon.svg`, `js/roster.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/render.js`, `js/game.js`, `js/main.js`.
- Procedurally drawn arena (obsidian colosseum, braziers, cracks, emblem, embers) and animated muscular rooster champions with team accents, tails, combs, weapons, health bars, player marker.
- Combat, lava pools, piercing plumes, burn, AI (targeting, strafing, dodging, specials), respawns, scoring, kill feed, announcements, results/rematch flow.
- Procedural WebAudio sound effects.
- Fixed a critical save/restore imbalance in `drawChampion` that broke the camera transform after the first unit.
- Rebalanced combat speed (HP/damage/cooldowns; timer 150s) and redesigned lava pool art and kill feed.
- Verified desktop rendering at 1440×900; all 8 fighters now render inside the arena.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay polish after latest changes; mobile HUD and touch controls not yet verified.
- Latest test state: desktop game screenshot shows all 8 fighters, new lava colors, and updated HUD; no console errors except earlier favicon 404 (favicon now added).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and test desktop gameplay: confirm no JS errors, kills accumulate at a reasonable pace, player input/aim/fire/dash/special work.
2. Test mobile viewport (390×844): menu layout, dual joysticks, ability buttons, HUD fit and safe areas; fix overlaps.
3. Test game-over/rematch and "Cambiar gallo" flow; verify round timer and score-to-10 ending.
4. Remove debug instrumentation exposure if desired (`window.__gallos` is intentional for automated checks), then run final desktop/mobile screenshots.
5. Optionally update `README.md` with game description and controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: menu, fighter-card container, result overlay, canvas.
- `style.css`: menu/result styling, responsive rules, safe-area vars.
- `js/roster.js`: world constants, role stats, team colors, fighter palettes/spawns.
- `js/render.js`: arena, champion, projectile, pool, particle, HUD rendering (save/restore was fixed).
- `js/game.js`: simulation, combat, pools, AI, scoring, round/timer logic.
- `js/main.js`: boot, resize/camera, input (mouse/keyboard/touch), menu/result wiring, loop.
- `js/audio.js`: synthesized SFX.
- `favicon.svg`: eliminates favicon 404.

## Important Context
- Server currently running in tmux session `game` at `http://localhost:3002` (Python `http.server`).
- Playwright CLI works only after symlinking browser revisions: `chromium-1243 → chromium-1248` and `chromium_headless_shell-1243 → chromium_headless_shell-1248` under `~/.cache/ms-playwright`.
- Playwright current viewport was resized to 1440×900; automated capture uses 1440×900 desktop and 390×844 mobile.
- Auto-capture clicks the button whose accessible name matches `/^(start|play)( game|now)?$/i`; `#playBtn` has `aria-label="Play"`.
- Latest screenshot: `screenshots/game6.png` shows correct 4v4 arena and HUD; timer reads 2:29.
- `drawChampion` must keep balanced save/restore (the extra final `ctx.restore()` was removed).
- Changes are uncommitted in git.
